Vanessa / Marissa — reviewed the redlines and attached the counsel summary (see below). High-level guidance: we can accept many commercial asks but will push back on a few legal exposure items.

Counsel summary (key points):
1) Subprocessors / notice period
- Chronicle requests 30 days notice for new subprocessors and effective consent window. Our standard is: prior notice + objection right within 15 days, with emergency exception (shorter notice) for operational continuity.
- Recommendation: Offer 30 days for non-emergency additions but keep 15-day objection right to align with current workflow. Provide a commitment to post an updated subprocessor inventory and a 30-day notice for major category changes.

2) Cross-border transfers
- Their draft requires "SCCs or equivalent safeguards" with specific technical measures. We already support SCCs and have an internal EU-hosting option.
- Recommendation: Accept SCCs; add language referencing our Transfer Addendum (link) that outlines available safeguards (SCCs, EU hosting, contractual commitments, encryption-in-transit & at-rest). Do not accept open-ended indemnities tied to transfer law changes.

3) Retention carveouts (logs & backups)
- Chronicle wants explicit carveouts to retain audit logs and backups beyond primary retention periods. This could increase risk if logs contain personal data.
- Recommendation: Offer limited carveout language: retain logs/backups for up to 90 days for incident investigation and regulatory needs; for longer retention, require documented justification and limited access controls.

4) Data deletion and evidence requests
- They asked for deletion certificates and ad-hoc evidence on backups. We can provide deletion confirmation for primary systems; for immutable backups provide schedule and process documentation. Avoid bespoke deletion certificates per request due to operational overhead.

5) Insurance / liability caps
- Their proposed liability lift for data incidents to unlimited for certain categories. Push back: maintain existing commercial liability cap (as per SOW/Order Form). Offer to increase cap for specific contractual commitments (e.g., data breaches with proven Redwood fault) subject to procurement exec approval.

6) Execution mechanics (DocuSign / AdobeSign)
- Chronicle prefers DocuSign. Legal is fine with DocuSign E-sign but needs to confirm signatory delegate list and whether the DPA will be appended to the Master Services Agreement during DocuSign flow. Recommend single DocuSign envelope with both MSA and DPA attached; include a clause that executed DPA supersedes prior versions.

Suggested next steps:
- Vanessa: propose the alternative language below to Amanda today (short email + attached one-pager with the three proposed edits).
- Rafael: I'll prepare a redline with tracked changes that accepts SCCs, proposes the 15/30 compromise on subprocessors, and adds the 90-day backup carveout.
- Grace: confirm operational feasibility for deletion confirmations and backup schedule.

Draft language snippets (for Vanessa to include in reply):
- Subprocessors: "Redwood will provide notice of new subprocessors at least 30 days prior to material onboarding and maintain a publicly accessible subprocessor inventory. Customer may object within 15 days of notice; in the absence of objection, Redwood may proceed. Emergency subprocessors may be onboarded sooner with notice as soon as practicable and remediation commitments."
- Transfers: "Data transfers will be governed by applicable transfer mechanisms (e.g., SCCs) and Redwood's Transfer Addendum, available at [link]. Where Customer requires hosting within a specific geography, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide such hosting as an optional deployment."
- Backups & Logs: "Redwood may retain system logs and immutable backups for up to 90 days for security and operational purposes, with access limited to authorized personnel and used only for incident response and compliance obligations."

I'll attach the tracked redline by EOD. If Amanda wants a call, I'm available tomorrow 10:00–12:00 PST.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

Amanda — thanks for the quick turn. Appreciate the clarity on timing. Some quick points and a proposed path to execution so we can close in the two-week window: 

1) Subprocessor notice: Redwood accepts a 30-day notice for non-emergency subprocessors; to balance operational agility, we propose Customer objection rights within 15 days of notice and an emergency exception for rapid operational needs. We will publish our subprocessor inventory and notify you of major category changes 30 days in advance.

2) Transfers: Redwood accepts execution of SCCs or equivalent transfer mechanisms. We'll attach our Transfer Addendum to the DPA and include hosting options if Chronicle requires EU-only hosting for covered processing. 

3) Logs & backups: Redwood is willing to include a limited carveout to retain logs and immutable backups for up to 90 days for incident response and regulatory obligations. Longer retention can be considered with documented justification and tighter access controls.

4) Evidence & deletion: We can provide deletion confirmations for primary systems and documented backup schedules for immutable backups. For large or bespoke evidence requests, we may need to scope with your procurement/legal team to avoid operational overload.

5) Execution flow: we are happy to use DocuSign for signing. Our legal counsel proposes a single envelope that includes the MSA and the executed DPA. Rafael has prepared a tracked redline and will share the file; we'll also attach the Transfer Addendum link in the envelope.
